Policy description — not an observed application result
Ordinary, authorized, root, isolated, shared-UID and work-profile process views have not been measured by this read.
Module content uses VIEW or SPOOF according to UID and unmount policy. Isolated/app-zygote targets use SPOOF; non-app UIDs usually use VIEW. A root result cannot verify an ordinary app’s view.
Stealth filters relevant /dev directory entries for SPOOF targets when enabled. It is not the policy used by every hidden path.
User HIDE exempts root, authorized apps and the resolver process. Some storage services also have parent exemptions. This differs from module visibility policy.
Filtered mount information applies to isolated targets and non-authorized apps. Privileged/system/authorized tools can retain topology; this is separate from module content visibility.
Explicit Maps rules apply to eligible SPOOF targets when enabled. They change Maps rendering and identity, not mapped file contents. Other proxy handling can also apply.
Statfs handling uses mount-view policy and requires statfs and mount hiding to be configured, mount hiding available, and global SUMH enabled. Root/non-root alone is not enough to predict the result.
Kernel Build modifies initial-UTS strings. It does not use per-application visibility policy and does not rewrite existing cloned UTS namespaces.
Kernel debug controls logging machinery. Its active flag is not evidence of any application’s file or mount view.
Overlay attribute handling filters marked superblocks according to mount-view target policy. Its actual observer effect is not established by the six-control runtime sample.
This read does not establish a process-specific observer policy for this feature.
